claims.text: An active-learning machine-learned interatomic potential can accurately reproduce ab initio solid-state free energies near melting.
The proposed potential can accurately reproduce ab initio liquid-state free energies near melting.
The proposed method can retain vibrational-entropy contributions to free energy.
The proposed method can capture anharmonic contributions to free energy.
DFPT augmentation enables the potential to capture electron–vibration coupling.
A sparse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics data is sufficient to train the proposed framework when selected iteratively by active learning.
The trained potential reproduces the ab initio potential-energy surface.
The trained potential reproduces the ab initio vibrational density of states.
Active learning identifies critical configuration-space regions in which anharmonicity is pronounced.
Active learning identifies critical configuration-space regions in which electron–vibration effects are pronounced.
Incorporating DFPT benchmarks into the training loop iteratively improves the potential's representation of anharmonic and electron–vibration effects.
Targeted active learning and DFPT augmentation reduce the amount of extensive AIMD sampling required.
The approach will reduce computational cost by approximately a factor of 5–10 relative to full AIMD workflows.
For elemental and binary systems, the approach will achieve free-energy fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
The approach will robustly extend from elemental and binary systems to high-entropy alloys such as CoCrFeNi.
The proposed method is effective from approximately 0.8 times the melting temperature to temperatures above the melting point.
The proposed method is applicable across elemental metals, binary alloys, and multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Traditional explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations require extensive computational resources.
